001: Carlos, can you help me prepare the presentation for tomorrow?
Sure, Laura. What topic do you have to talk about?
About climate change in Spain. I have some data, but I don't know how to organize it.
We can start with a general idea and then give concrete examples.
Sounds good to me. Do you think I should include a lot of charts?
A couple of clear charts are enough. The important thing is that you explain each one well.
002: I can't find a good way to start my presentation.
You could begin with a question to grab their attention.
A question? I can't think of any interesting ones.
For example: how much water do you think we use per day?
That question is very visual. I'll use it to introduce the topic.
I'm glad it works for you. Then we'll continue with the main data.
003: Javier, do you have a moment to listen to my practice run?
Sure, I'm not in a hurry right now. Start whenever you want.
Okay, but let me know if I talk too fast.
I will. I'll also tell you if you need to pause.
Thanks. I prefer that you correct me during the rehearsal.
Perfect, that way you can improve before the real presentation.
004: I get nervous speaking in front of the whole class.
It's normal to feel that way. Have you already practiced out loud?
Only once, and I got stuck in the middle.
Practice will give you confidence. We can go over the script together.
That would help me a lot. Do you mind if we do it now?
That's what I'm here for. Let's review it calmly.
005: I don't know whether to use slides or write everything on the board.
Slides look clearer if you have images.
That's true, but I'm afraid the equipment will fail.
You can bring a printed copy just in case.
Good idea, that way I'll have an emergency plan.
And if something fails, breathe and keep going with what you know.
006: How much time do I have exactly for the presentation?
I think about ten minutes, and then there are questions.
Then I'll have to cut some examples so I don't go over.
Yes, better to come up short than to leave the topic half-finished.
And what do I do if someone interrupts me with a question?
You can say you'll answer it at the end if it's not urgent.
007: I've prepared the conclusion, but I don't know if it's too long.
Tell it to me and I'll give you my honest opinion.
I summarize the three main ideas and end with a reflection.
That sounds good, but try to keep it brief.
Do you think one strong final sentence is enough?
Yes, a good final sentence leaves a better impression than many words.
008: I feel embarrassed when everyone looks at me at the same time.
It happens to all of us at first. Look at a fixed point in the room.
And what if I go blank in the middle of the presentation?
Keep some small notes on hand to check without it being noticeable.
That will give me more confidence. Thanks for the advice.
You're welcome. You'll see that once you start, the nerves go away on their own.
009: Do you think I should memorize the whole speech?
You don't need to. It's better if you sound natural and spontaneous.
But if I don't memorize it, I'm afraid of forgetting something important.
You can remember the key ideas and explain them in your own words.
You're right, that way it will sound less artificial.
Exactly. Being natural connects better with whoever is listening to you.
010: In the end, I ended up with a pretty complete presentation.
I'm glad. Do you want to do one last rehearsal before tomorrow?
Yes, but this time timing myself to adjust the length.
Good idea. I'll keep track of the time and let you know if you go over.
Perfect. That will put my mind at ease.
I'm sure you'll do great. You've worked hard for this.
